Hi Sam / Acme security team,

Thanks for the intro call earlier — attaching a proposed onboarding plan and a network diagram for the VPC/on‑prem private deployment. High-level asks from our side so we can finalize the operator model and rollout window: 

- Confirm the operator scope you prefer: (A) Hardware-backed HSM operators with no exported key material, or (B) split-operator model where Redwood manages KMS proxies and Acme keeps key shards.
- Egress policy: we propose a single dedicated outbound bastion host for telemetry & attestation traffic to redwood-control.redwood-infra, with explicit firewall rules. Please confirm allowed egress endpoints/IPs.
- Key rotation windows: propose monthly soft-rotation (config/agent) + quarterly HSM seal rotations; need your blackout windows.
- Audit & attestation: we will deliver signed attestation blobs for each operator session and an S3 bucket for audit logs. Do you require SOC2-aware evidence or an independent attestation cert?

Attachments: operator_onboarding_checklist.pdf (step-by-step), private_deploy_network_diagram.vsdx, hsm-partitioning-matrix.xlsx.

Next steps: please review and reply with the preferred operator scope (A or B), and any constraints on egress endpoints by EOD Thu.

Thanks,
Soojin Lee

Soojin — thanks, this is helpful. A few clarifications from Acme Security: 

1) We want option B (split-operator). Primary requirement: Acme retains sole possession of key material at rest. Any operator actions that require unwrapping must be proven via multi-party attestation (two-person approval + HSM policy). 

2) Egress: we cannot allow direct outbound to third-party control planes except to a short list of IPs (please see inline firewall list). Our infra team will only permit outbound to: 52.12.34.65, 52.12.34.66, and api.redwood-infra.com (443) from the bastion.

3) Audit: we need daily digest with signed hashes and the raw audit stream for the first 90 days. SOC2 evidence is desirable; please include your SOC2 report or an alternative attestation mechanism.

Can you confirm that operator ephemeral tokens will never be persisted on disk and that operator sessions are limited to 8 hours TTL? Also, we need a proof-of-concept run at the staging/acceptance VPC before production.

—Sam

Thanks Sam — acknowledging the constraints and adding technical details so ops/infra can sign off: 

- Split-operator model (B) implementation notes: 
  * Acme holds the primary key shards in HSM partitions under customer-controlled KMS labels. Redwood runs a KMS proxy in the private VPC that never has access to raw key material; it only receives wrapped tokens.
  * We will use an asymmetric sealing key pair on the HSM: operator sessions request an ephemeral session key which is wrapped to Acme's shard; unwrap requires a quorum: HSM policy + operator mTLS cert + Acme approve.

- Operator session model: 
  * Ephemeral session tokens (JWT-style) minted by Redwood's control plane with a TTL of 8 hours by default; strict in-memory only on the bastion; we will enforce no-disk persistence via tmpfs and kernel-level mount flags.
  * Each session generates a signed attestation envelope (COSE) containing session metadata and HSM signature. Envelopes are pushed to the audit bucket and mirrored to Acme's audit collector.

- Networking & egress: 
  * Single outbound bastion (egress proxy) sits in the DMZ with explicit firewall rules limiting outbound to the three Acme-approved endpoints. All attestation and metric telemetry must go through this host.
  * Mutual TLS for the control channel; we will rotate mTLS certs quarterly and publish CRLs to your designated endpoint.

- Rotation and emergency zeroize: 
  * Configuration rotation (key labels, metadata) — monthly soft rotations.
  * HSM re-seal (policy rotation) — quarterly, scheduled two-week maintenance windows. 
  * Emergency zeroize playbook: operator executes zeroize via a multi-authorized HSM command; we will provide a signed audit and a separate out-of-band verification token.

Attachments: updated_network_diagram_v2 (in Drive link) and hsm-partitioning-matrix.xlsx. Please confirm staging date so SRE can schedule the runbook rehearsal.

-Karthik

2) Evidence package: Sam — we can provide our SOC2 Type II summary and the HSM attestation chain from our vendor, but Acme must execute the data processing addendum for on‑prem telemetry forwarding.

Thanks everyone — summarizing agreed decisions and next steps: 

Agreed decisions:
- Operator model: Option B (split-operator) — Acme retains key shards in HSM partitions; Redwood KMS proxy handles wrapped requests only.
- Operator sessions: ephemeral tokens, 8-hour TTL, in-memory only on the bastion + signed COSE attestation envelopes mirrored to Acme.
- Egress policy: single outbound bastion with firewall to 52.12.34.65, 52.12.34.66, api.redwood-infra.com:443.
- Rotation cadence: monthly soft rotations; quarterly HSM policy reseal; emergency zeroize with multi-authorized HSM command.
- Evidence: Redwood to share SOC2 Type II summary + HSM vendor attestation. Acme to finalize DPA and escrow addendum.

Immediate next steps (owners):
- Vanessa: circulate escrow redline and push legal/procurement (due: 2026-10-06).
- Karthik: publish staging runbook and updated network diagram to the Confluence link; schedule SRE rehearsal (target: 2026-10-20).
- Soojin: bundle SOC2 summary + attestation artifacts and upload to the evidence Drive folder (due: 2026-10-05).
- Sam/Acme: approve the three egress IPs and confirm blackout windows for production (due: 2026-10-06).

If there are no objections I will update the onboarding checklist and lock the staging date.

Thanks — good progress.
Soojin
